## Step 5 spot-check results

**Methodology:** Targeted grep across 6 high-risk pattern classes (forgotten TODOs, "DO NOT" warnings, personal identifiers, tracked IDE/screenshot dirs, real emails, private-context mentions).

**Findings:**

| Class | Hits | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 1. TODO/FIXME with sensitive context | All Laravel `remember()` cache method + `remember_token` columns + documented `TEMPORARY_UNAUTHENTICATED_API_*` allowlist | ✅ Clean |
| 2. "Do not" warnings | 2 tax/legal "do not deploy real money" advisories | ✅ Clean |
| 3. Personal identifier shapes | **Notable** — `SETUP.md` references `melnick`/`spirit`/`jdtogni` nicknames | ⚠️ See below |
| 4. Tracked screenshots/.idea/.vscode | None found | ✅ Clean |
| 5. Real-looking emails outside known sets | All hits are OSS author addrs (Taylor Otwell, barryvdh), service test addrs, or synthetic fixtures | ✅ Clean |
| 6. Private-context in LICENSE/README/AGENTS | All acceptable: GPLv3 standard text, generic bastion topology, OK references to "private secrets repo" | ✅ Clean |

**The one notable finding:** `SETUP.md` documents the personal homelab topology — `melnick` (Synology NAS, GPG bundle source), `spirit` (prod server), ssh as `jdtogni`. The IPs are already redacted as `REDACTED_NAS_HOST` / `REDACTED_PROD_HOST` placeholders, so no direct credentials leak. What does leak: the nicknames and the fact that the user runs a Synology NAS as part of the dev workflow. Low credential risk; some personal-context exposure.

## My recommendation
Proceed to first sync — the spot-check is otherwise clean, this is the 3rd audit pass, your stance on rollback is relaxed. The `SETUP.md` hostnames are uncomfortable-not-dangerous; can be scrubbed in a follow-up commit if you want, or shipped as-is.
